sources.entry: PageExtender - Extend pages with your own CSS and JS files.

summary.one_liner: PageExtender is a Safari extension for macOS that injects your own CSS and JavaScript files into web pages.
summary.what_it_does: The README is very short and gives only a tagline: extend pages with your own CSS and JS files. It is described as a Safari app, and the README links to an announcement blog post and a Mac App Store listing. It says the software can be run for free from the published source, and that donations are appreciated. The README does not describe configuration, file-matching rules, or how scripts are loaded, so those details are not covered here.
use_cases: customize how websites look in Safari
add custom CSS to web pages
tweak websites with personal style or script files
how_to_run: Buy the app on the Mac App Store ($5)
Or build from the published source code (README gives no build steps)
notable: Injects user-supplied CSS and JS files into pages in Safari
Source code is published, so it can be run for free
Also sold on the Mac App Store for $5
caveats: README is very short and gives no setup or usage instructions
Paid version on the Mac App Store ($5); free option is building from source
Safari and macOS only, as far as the README indicates
